newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Ruth Richardson to be acting chair of Dairy Brands.
newsitem.headline: Ruth Richardson to be acting chair of Dairy Brands.

text.p: Former finance minister Ruth Richardson will take over as acting chairwoman of listed dairy company Dairy Brands following the resignation of chairman Murray Valentine, the New Zealand Press Association reported on Monday.
Dairy Brands secretary Simon Challies said Richardson would chair the annual meeting later this month. A decision on who would head the board would be made in the New Year.
Dairy brands earlier this month reported a 91.7 percent plunge in bottom-line profit to $249,000 for the year to September, from $3.01 million for the previous 12 months.

In the annual report, reasons given for failure to meet the projected $3.82 million surplus (excluding fixed-asset sales) included the fact that development of new dairy products did not proceed due to the emphasis on ice cream production.
Dairy farm assets, expected in the prospectus to be revalued, were not revalued due to a change in farm valuation policy.

In the report, Valentine said milk production was significantly up as the mid-season approached, compared with the corresponding period in 1995. The current season had returned to normal growth patterns, compared with a harsh winter in 1995
with reduced spring grass growth which caused feed prices to rise.
The Dairy Board has projected a lower payout this season. Although this was disappointing, the medium to long-term outlook remained positive.
Valentine said the consumer foods division had an indifferent first year, but the board was confident that processing and marketing dairy products was the group's correct strategy.
Efforts have been made to concentrate on sales, marketing, and distribution of the Killinchy Gold brand ice cream in the Auckland region, which had produced increased sales.
